title: Unit-econ dashboard: query perf (pre-aggregations, result caching, high-cardinality guardrails)
author: Thomas Baird
description: Context: The unit economics dashboard drilldowns (model/region/tier + optional runtime_config/quantization_profile) were timing out under internal demo load and were easy to accidentally blow up with high-cardinality filters (e.g., unbounded runtime_config, long date ranges). This PR introduces three changes: (1) pre-aggregated rollups for the most common query shapes, (2) API-layer result caching keyed by a normalized query spec, and (3) guardrails that reject/shape queries likely to trigger expensive scans or runaway cardinality. Motivation: keep p95 < 800ms for default dashboard views and protect ClickHouse from ad-hoc exploration patterns while we iterate on V2 drilldowns. Implementation details: Pre-aggregations: add daily rollup tables/materialized views for unit-econ slices used by Console: by (date, model_family, model_variant, region, customer_tier) and by (date, model_family, region, customer_tier). The query planner in unit-econ-service now routes requests to rollups when the requested dimensions match (or are a subset) and the time grain is daily. For queries needing runtime_config or quantization_profile, we keep the base fact-derived aggregation but apply stricter limits (see guardrails). Result cache: add Redis-backed cache in unit-econ-service (QueryCache) with TTLs: 60s for parameterized time-series and 5m for table exports at daily grain. Cache keys are based on: metric_name + normalized date_range (rounded to day for daily queries) + selected dimensions + filters + pagination. Includes cache bypass header for debugging: X-Redwood-Bypass-Cache: true (internal only) and emits cache hit/miss metrics. Guardrails: enforce max date range = 120 days (hard), default max = 30 days unless the request is from an internal role and uses rollups; require at least one of {model_family, region, customer_tier} when requesting breakdown tables; restrict high-cardinality dimensions: runtime_config and quantization_profile are only allowed when (a) date range <= 14 days and (b) one of model_variant or region is specified; cap returned groups (topK) to 200 with explicit order-by blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens desc for deterministic truncation; add clear error messages surfaced to Console so users know how to refine filters. Query changes are backwards-compatible at the API contract level; behavior change is that previously-accepted expensive queries now return 400 with guidance. Observability: add metrics unit_econ_query_latency_ms (p50/p95), unit_econ_query_cache_hit_ratio, unit_econ_query_rejected_total (tagged by reason), and include the resolved query plan (rollup vs base) as a tag. Testing/validation: unit tests for query normalization and guardrail rules; integration test that compares rollup vs base aggregation results on a sampled day partition (tolerance 0 for deterministic rollups); load test locally with 50 concurrent dashboard sessions: p95 for default time-series improved from ~3.8s to ~420ms; ClickHouse CPU down ~55% for the same workload. Rollout: behind server flag unit_econ_query_perf_v1 (default on in staging, off in prod until Console rollout flag flips); once enabled, we’ll monitor cache hit ratio and rejected queries to ensure UX doesn’t regress. Follow-ups: (a) consider weekly rollups for long-range Finance views, (b) add per-endpoint query cost budgeting (max rows read), (c) coordinate with Design on error copy in empty/error states. Screenshots: n/a (backend-only; Console will pick up faster responses automatically).
commits: perf(unit-econ): add daily rollup materialized views for common drilldowns
perf(unit-econ): route queries to rollups when dimensions/timegrain match
perf(api): add redis query result cache + normalized cache keys
perf(api): add guardrails for date range and high-cardinality filters
obs(unit-econ): emit cache hit/miss + rejected query metrics
test(unit-econ): rollup/base equivalence + guardrail unit tests
review_conversation: Logan Wright: Pre-agg routing looks good. Can we make sure we don’t accidentally route to rollups when quantization_profile is requested (since rollups don’t include it)? Also please add a metric tag for which plan was used.
Thomas Baird (author): Good call — added explicit exclusion for runtime_config/quantization_profile and included query_plan=rollup|base tag on latency metric.
Chloe Martin: On guardrails: returning 400 is fine, but Console needs a stable error code and message to show guidance. Can we standardize the error payload and include a reason enum?

Thomas Baird (author): Added UnitEconQueryRejectedError with reason values (DATE_RANGE_TOO_LARGE, MISSING_REQUIRED_DIMENSION, HIGH_CARDINALITY_DIM_REQUIRES_NARROWER_SLICE, GROUP_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) and kept message text user-readable.

Caleb Johnson: Please confirm rollups match the semantic layer definitions from PR-11857 (column names + grain). Also, do we have a reconciliation test to ensure rollups are exact equals of base for a sample partition?
Thomas Baird (author): Updated rollup view names/columns to match semantic layer conventions and added an integration test that compares results for a sampled day for the default dimension set.

Allison Grant: Cache TTLs: 60s seems fine, but please add metrics for hit ratio and a way to bypass cache for debugging incidents. Also make sure cache is disabled for requests with internal debug headers that might change output.

Thomas Baird (author): Added cache hit/miss counters + hit ratio dashboard metric, and X-Redwood-Bypass-Cache=true internal header. Cache key normalization ignores debug headers and we bypass caching when bypass is present.
Felix Schneider: Minor: can we cap max page_size to prevent someone exporting huge tables via the API and blowing memory? Also pagination + cache key needs to include page token/offset.
Thomas Baird (author): Added page_size max=500 and included pagination params in the cache key. Also ensured we only cache successful 200 responses (no caching for 4xx/5xx).
Logan Wright: Approved after latest changes. Thanks for adding plan tag + equivalence test.
Chloe Martin: Approved. I’ll coordinate with DES-211 for error state copy.
Allison Grant: Approved (please remind oncall to use bypass header if debugging).
release_notes: Improves unit economics dashboard query latency via daily rollups and API result caching
Adds guardrails for high-cardinality filters and excessive date ranges to protect analytics cluster
Adds metrics for query plan selection, cache hit ratio, and rejected-query reasons
